title: Google Gemini Crosses 1 Billion Users, Becoming Company's Fastest-Growing Product
excerpt: The AI assistant has matched ChatGPT at billion-user scale in a matter of weeks, as the market share race between Google and OpenAI intensifies across consumer and enterprise applications.
body:
• Google's Gemini app has crossed 1 billion monthly active users, making it the company's fastest-growing product and joining an exclusive club that includes Search, Gmail, YouTube, and Chrome.
  • The milestone comes as ChatGPT also reached 1 billion monthly users in June, intensifying the head-to-head race between Google and OpenAI in the AI assistant market.
  • ChatGPT's market share among AI assistants fell below 50% for the first time in H1 2026, according to Sensor Tower, while Gemini's share rose to 27.7%.
  • Nearly 90% of Fortune 100 companies now use Gemini Enterprise, and Google's AI models process 22 billion tokens per minute across its platforms.

Google's Gemini app has officially crossed 1 billion monthly active users, becoming the fastest-growing product in the company's history and placing it in a dead heat with OpenAI's ChatGPT atop the global AI assistant market.

The milestone caps a year of explosive growth. At Google I/O in May 2025, Gemini had 400 million monthly users. That figure climbed to 650 million by October, 750 million by February, and 950 million at the company's Q2 2026 earnings call on July 22. Daily active users have tripled over the past 12 months.

The Race to a Billion

The AI assistant market is now defined by two products at billion-user scale. OpenAI's ChatGPT reached that threshold in June, becoming what the company called the fastest product ever to hit the mark. Google's Gemini has matched it within weeks, fueled by deep integration across Android's 3 billion-plus devices and aggressive expansion on iOS.

https://x.com/Google/status/2087232072481939470

"Users love new agentic features like Daily Brief and our personalized agent, Gemini Spark, which is now available in the U.S. and internationally. We've been shipping helpful new features like this at an incredible pace."

— Sundar Pichai, CEO, Alphabet

The Gemini app has been downloaded more than 137 million times on iOS in the past year, according to AppFigures. Features like the Nano Banana image generation model have helped Google penetrate Apple's ecosystem, an arena where ChatGPT has historically dominated among AI chatbot apps.

Shifting Market Dynamics

The competitive landscape is tilting. Sensor Tower's "State of AI" report for H1 2026 found that ChatGPT's market share among AI assistants fell below 50% for the first time, while Gemini's share rose to 27.7%. The data suggests a market that is diversifying fast, with neither player holding unchallenged dominance.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=NUHqKkvq17I

Google's advantage lies in distribution. Gemini is embedded across Search, YouTube, Google Cloud, coding tools, and the company's advertising platform. Its AI Mode feature in Search — a Q&A-style interface powered by Gemini models — has independently crossed 1 billion monthly users and is driving "an incremental increase" in search queries, according to Google.

On the enterprise side, nearly 90% of Fortune 100 companies now use Gemini Enterprise. Google's AI models process approximately 22 billion tokens per minute, up from 16 billion the previous quarter, reflecting surging demand across consumer and business applications.

The Revenue Machine Behind the Growth

The user surge arrives alongside strong financial results for Alphabet. The company reported 24% year-over-year revenue growth in Q2 2026, with total revenue reaching $119.8 billion. Google Cloud revenue jumped 82% to nearly $25 billion, with a cloud backlog of $514 billion signaling sustained enterprise demand for AI infrastructure.

But the growth has not been frictionless. Google delayed the launch of its flagship Gemini 3.5 Pro model due to shortcomings in coding and agentic tasks, Reuters reported. The delay raised questions about whether Google can match the pace of rivals in the lucrative AI coding assistant market, even as its consumer-facing products surge ahead.

What's Next

Google has expanded its model portfolio with the launch of Gemini 3.6 Flash, Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite, and Gemini 3.5 Flash Cyber, while work on its next-generation Gemini 4 model is underway. The company has also rebranded NotebookLM as Gemini Notebook, consolidating its AI product lineup under the Gemini umbrella.

For the broader AI industry, the simultaneous arrival of two billion-user products signals that AI assistants have moved from novelty to mainstream utility. The question now is whether the market will sustain two dominant platforms or whether distribution advantages and enterprise adoption will eventually tip the balance.
